title: Dissolving and Solutions
seo_title: Year 5 Science: Dissolving and Solutions Worksheets (Soluble, Insoluble, Saturated)
standard_code: Year 5: Properties and changes of materials
standard_text: Know that some materials will dissolve in liquid to form a solution, and describe how to recover a substance from a solution.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on dissolving: soluble and insoluble materials, solute, solvent and solution, what speeds up dissolving, saturated solutions and conservation of mass. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The solute spreads through the solvent; heat, stirring and small pieces speed it up.
body_html:
How to think about it

Soluble materials dissolve to make a solution; insoluble ones do not.

  • Solute (what dissolves) + solvent (the liquid) = solution. The solute is still there, just in tiny pieces.
  • Warmer water, stirring and smaller pieces make dissolving faster. A saturated solution can dissolve no more.
  • Mass is kept: 100 g water + 10 g salt = 110 g. Evaporating the water gets the solid back.
Example

200 g water + 15 g sugar. Mass of solution?

Nothing is lost

Answer: 215 g

Example

Sugar cube or caster sugar: faster?

Smaller pieces dissolve faster

Answer: caster sugar

Common mistakes

  • Thinking dissolved sugar has disappeared.
  • Confusing dissolving with melting.
  • Thinking mass goes down when something dissolves.

faq.a: It breaks into pieces too small to see and spreads through the liquid. It is still there: you can taste it and get it back by evaporating the water.

faq.q: How can you make sugar dissolve faster?
faq.a: Use warmer water, stir it, or use smaller pieces such as caster sugar instead of sugar cubes.

faq.q: Does mass change when something dissolves?
faq.a: No. The mass of the solution equals the mass of the water plus the mass of the solid that dissolved.
